articles.title: “Been tackled on concrete”: Dak Prescott dismisses Maracana surface concerns
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys are preparing for one of the most unique road trips in franchise history
articles.summary: The Cowboys are preparing for one of the most unique road trips in franchise history
articles.body:
As questions continue to swirl around the condition of the playing surface at Rio de Janeiro's iconic Maracaña Stadium, Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott appears to have little interest in joining the debate.

Ahead of Sunday's highly anticipated matchup between the Cowboys and Baltimore Ravens, Prescott delivered a memorable response when asked about concerns surrounding the grass field that has drawn attention throughout the week. "Not a lot goes into that for me. I trust my equipment, the cleats that I'm going to have," Dak said. "Not really even looking into the news about how people feel about the field. If it's the surface we're going to play on, let's go do it."

Then came the quote that quickly captured attention. "Where I'm from, I've played on worse. Been tackled on concrete. So the fact that the grass is soft, we'll take it, I'll take it anyways. I hope not to hit it anyways." The comments reflect the mindset Prescott has carried throughout his NFL career.

While others have focused on reports regarding the stadium's turf conditions, the veteran quarterback has maintained confidence that the league would not allow the game to proceed if the field were unsafe. His head coach, Brian Schottenheimer, has expressed similar confidence throughout the week as Dallas prepares for one of the most unique road trips in franchise history.

A milestone moment for Prescott

The trip to Brazil r epresents more than just another regular-season game. For the first time in his 11 NFL seasons, Prescott will play an international game, adding another milestone to a career that has already included multiple playoff appearances, Pro Bowls and countless high-profile moments.

The Cowboys arrived in Rio de Janeiro on Friday before holding practice at Flamengo's training facility, one of the most recognizable sports venues in Brazil. For Prescott, the experience has provided an opportunity to reflect on how far both he and the NFL have come .

"Surprised it's been this long, but excited it's here and it's in Brazil for the first time, a place I've never been," Prescott said. "Obviously just trying to expand the game to all the different places." The quarterback understands that Sunday's contest is about more than two teams battling for a victory. It is also part of the NFL's broader effort to grow the sport internationally and introduce new audiences to American football.

The Cowboys' global appeal

Few franchises are better positioned to help that mission than the Cowboys. Prescott acknowledged that one of the unique aspects of playing for Dallas is the team's enormous worldwide following. No matter where the Cowboys travel, they are likely to find fans wearing the star logo.

"I don't know if there's any place in the world that there's not a good bit of Cowboys fans," Prescott said. "That's the awesome part about playing for this organization." The quarterback added that he hopes Brazilian fans attending the game will have an opportunity to experience Cowboys football firsthand, perhaps for the first time.

That responsibility is something Prescott says he thinks about regularly. "It's something that I think about each and every game, is 'Who's watching for the first time?' Or, 'Who's trying to pick up this game, and how can I inspire them?'"

Of course, while the international spotlight and field discussions have dominated headlines, the Cowboys still have a difficult football challenge waiting for them. The Ravens arrive in Rio with one of the NFL's most talented rosters, making Sunday's matchup one of the marquee games of the early season.

articles.title: Cowboys and Ravens set to play on a "dog s**t" playing surface at the iconic Maracanã Stadium
articles.standfirst: The field at the Maracanã is usually in tip-top shape for major soccer events, but it doesn't look prepared for an NFL game.
articles.summary: The field at the Maracanã is usually in tip-top shape for major soccer events, but it doesn't look prepared for an NFL game.
articles.body:
There are already plenty of reasons for why NFL players don't like the idea of playing international games during the regular season. The biggest reason is the brutal travel schedule that throws off the team's routine. But in Week 3, there's a different reason emerging.

The Dallas Cowboys and Baltimore Raven s are scheduled to play at the famous Maracanã Stadium in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil on Sunday. In theory, it should be a spectacular event. But once the players got to the stadium this week, it became clear that there are issues.

The biggest issue is quite clearly the state of the playing surface at the stadium. Usually in great shape for soccer games, since Flamengo and Fluminense both play their matches there, the Cowboys and Ravens have both expressed concern about the playing field.

Groundskeepers at the stadium had to apply synthetic fiber to the field just days before the game in order to reinforce the playing surface, since the field has been hit by heavy rainfall recently.

The field at the Maracanã is still in very bad shape as NFL game nears

Media members got a close-up look at the field the day before the game, and according to one source for Pro Football Talk, the field " looks like dog s**t ".

Hopefully, there will be no injuries as a result of the shape of the field. What's clear is that both teams could be at a disadvantage, given that they've never played on anything similar in the past.

articles.title: Ravens vs Cowboys: Where to watch today's international game and what time it starts in the United States
articles.standfirst: Cowboys and Ravens bring the NFL to the Maracanã with a showdown of red-hot offenses in Rio
articles.summary: Cowboys and Ravens bring the NFL to the Maracanã with a showdown of red-hot offenses in Rio
articles.body:
The NFL crosses the halfway point once again with one of the most eye-catching stops of this year’s season. The Dallas Cowboys and the Baltimore Ravens will headline the Week 3 international game , and they will do so not in Texas or Maryland, but at the legendary Maracanã Stadium in Rio de Janeiro , which has a capacity of 78,838 fans.

It is a clash between two conferences, two philosophies, and two teams that need to correct course before their starts become complicated.

What time does the Cowboys game start and where to watch it in the United States?

The matchup is scheduled for this Sunday, September 27, 2026 . In the United States, the initial kickoff is set for the early afternoon hours on Sunday:

Dallas and Baltimore fans will be able to follow it through the league’s usual broadcast schedule: CBS on television and Paramount+ via streaming. As always, it’s a good idea to check local listings to confirm the broadcast in the respective cities.

How are the Cowboys and Ravens arriving at the Maracanã?

Both teams started the season with a 1-1 record, but with very different feelings. The Cowboys fell in Week 1 to the New York Giants 20-28 on the road, and responded in Week 2 with a 37-20 blowout over the Washington Commanders at home.

In two games they have totaled 57 points for and 48 against, a +9 differential that reflects a productive offense but a defense still needing fine-tuning. In the overall NFL standings, Dallas sits in 20th place out of 32, and in the NFC East it is third, behind Philadelphia and those same Giants who already beat them.

The Ravens, meanwhile, got off to a strong start with a 41-23 road win over the Indianapolis Colts , but stumbled in Week 2 by losing 17-24 at home to the New Orleans Saints.

With 58 points scored and 47 conceded (+11), Baltimore is 19th in the overall standings and second in the AFC North, behind the undefeated Cincinnati Bengals. The loss to New Orleans raised alarm bells, especially because of the lopsided offense they displayed in their opener.

This is a clash of offenses that know how to put points on the board. Baltimore's 58 and Dallas's 57 in just two games foreshadow a high-tempo game, something the market has read clearly: the total line is set between 52.5 and 53 points, one of the highest figures of the week.

The key will be which of the two defenses manages to make a stop first: Dallas has allowed 48 points and Baltimore 47, nearly identical numbers that suggest neither side has solved that issue yet.

The "neutral field" factor adds an extra layer of uncertainty. Neither Dallas nor Baltimore will enjoy their true home turf at the Maracanã, an unprecedented venue that levels the logistical and environmental conditions for both squads.

Implications for the playoff race

Although we are in Week 3, every result is already starting to weigh heavily. In the AFC North, Baltimore needs to win so as not to fall behind Bengals team that started 2-0. A victory would put the Ravens back on the path of a roster that last season reached the Divisional Round of the playoffs.

For Dallas, which in the NFC East already carries an internal divisional loss to the Giants, beating a rival from another conference would be an emotional boost and a valuable tiebreaker in the wild-card race. Both teams hover around the lower middle of the overall standings (positions 19 and 20), so this is the kind of game that can reshape perceptions.

What the betting market says about the game in Brazil and our prediction for Ravens vs Cowboys

Bettors have installed the Ravens as clear favorites. The moneyline gives Baltimore an implied probability of 61.6% (odds of 1.59), compared to the Cowboys’ 38.4% (odds of 2.62).

In the point spread, Baltimore appears as the -3 to -3.5 favorite, with Dallas getting those same points as an advantage. It is a tight margin that acknowledges the Texans' offensive potential even as support leans toward Baltimore.

Everything points to a high-scoring game. With two offenses averaging close to 29 points per game and defenses that are still vulnerable, the most logical bet is that the score shoots toward (or above) that 52.5-53 line.

Baltimore comes in as the favorite because of its higher offensive ceiling and recent postseason experience , but Dallas has the firepower to turn this into an open shootout. I’m leaning toward a narrow Ravens victory, in a matchup that will most likely be decided in the fourth quarter and that the Maracanã will remember for a long time.

articles.title: Brian Schottenheimer's wife falls ill in Dallas while the Cowboys play the Ravens in Brazil
articles.standfirst: Schottenheimer had said the trip to Rio de Janeiro must be about football and only football
articles.summary: Schottenheimer had said the trip to Rio de Janeiro must be about football and only football
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer made the trip to Brazil with football as his sole focus, but his wife, Gemmi , remained back in Dallas after falling ill with the flu.

Schottenheimer and the Cowboys departed Dallas on Thursday for their Week 3 matchup with the Baltimore Ravens in Rio de Janeiro, leaving their families behind as part of a deliberate decision to keep the team focused on football.

While Schottenheimer prepared for his first international game as Cowboys head coach, Gemmi stayed home and shared an update on social media about an eventful weekend that left her missing the family.

“Not my weekend…flat tire to under the weather… I miss you @savannahschottenheimer,” Gemmi Schottenheimer posted on her Instagram story alongside a photo of herself.

Savannah is the couple's daughter and attends Auburn University. Brian and Gemmi also have a son, with both children now away from home.

Schottenheimer had previously explained that the Cowboys ' trip was being treated strictly as a football operation, with the team avoiding the tourist activities that might normally accompany an international trip.

“We’re going to be busy. This is a business trip,” Schottenheimer said. “The meetings and the walkthroughs and the practice that we’ll have [Friday], the trip to the stadium on Saturday, those are all critical parts to what we’re doing so we go into the game feeling prepared.

“I’m not planning any touristy attractions. My thing is to focus on getting down there. It’s going to be a long trip. We know that. We own that. Got a good plan in place.”

Field for Brazil’s NFL game raises concerns

The Cowboys arrived in Brazil with a 1-1 record for a matchup that marks the NFL's first game in Rio de Janeiro as the Ravens enter the contest with their own expectations, while the condition of Maracana Stadium's field has emerged as another storyline.

Images and videos from the stadium showed areas of patchy grass ahead of kickoff, prompting concerns from the NFL Players Association about player safety and the quality of the playing surface.

JC Tretter addressed those concerns publicly but the NFL field director Nick Pappas later said the surface had passed the necessary tests as he aimed to calm worries that the pitch could be dangerous to the players.

He pointed out that an independent inspector and an NFLPA representative were both involved in Friday's assessment and Pappas also explained that synthetic fibers had been added to the grass using a Grassmaster Stitching machine in an effort to reinforce the surface and provide additional stability.

Schottenheimer 's attention remains on preparing Dallas for Baltimore, but his wife's update provides a reminder of how hard it can be to leave home affairs at home after the Cowboys ' coach insisted the trip would be about football.

articles.title: Dak Prescott ‘removes’ ex-fiancée Sarah Jane Ramos from latest post following allegations of infidelity
articles.standfirst: Ramos recently accused Prescott of repeatedly cheating, while the quarterback has kept public focus on their children
articles.summary: Ramos recently accused Prescott of repeatedly cheating, while the quarterback has kept public focus on their children
articles.body:
D ak Prescott ’s latest family post was simple on the surface as a father celebrating his two daughters. The timing, however, placed it squarely in the middle of renewed attention on his breakup with former fiancée Sarah Jane Ramos .

Prescott marked National Daughter’s Day by sharing photos of Margaret Jane Rose and Aurora Rayne on Instagram, writing: “Happy National Daughter’s Day, Daddy loves you, Girls 4ever.”

Ramos , the girls’ mother, didn't appear in the post. That absence comes only days after she publicly made her strongest accusation yet about the end of their relationship, claiming she had been “cheated on repeatedly.” Prescott hasn't responded directly to that allegation.

The latest round of attention began when a social-media account speculated that Ramos might be pregnant. She quickly rejected the claim.

“Hi everyone. Not pregnant!! Just very thick, eating again, and happier than I’ve been in a long time!” Ramos wrote. “That’s usually what happens when you aren’t getting cheated on repeatedly and finally leave a situation that makes you unhappy.”

Ramos also criticized the level of scrutiny around her life, writing: “I suggest all of you find something else to do with your free time because being this concerned with what I’m up to and if I’m pregnant is high key very weird and I’m pretty sure most of you need therapy.”

Her comments were the clearest public allegation of infidelity to emerge from either side since the engagement ended.

Prescott pushed back about the breakup

Prescott and Ramos split in March, only weeks before they were expected to marry. Reports around the breakup included claims of tension during a trip to the Bahamas and allegations that Prescott had communicated with other women.

When he addressed the split in August, he focused instead on what he called misinformation.

“There were a lot of false narratives out there on both of our sides,” Prescott said. “Yeah, it was an unfortunate situation for obviously everybody. More importantly, the kids. And so for me, it’s just about making sure I’m there in every which way for them.”

Daughters remain central point of contact

Prescott and Ramos were first linked in 2023 and are parents to Margaret and Aurora. Despite the breakup, the two have continued to appear committed to co-parenting.

They have reportedly come together for family occasions, including their younger daughter’s birthday, and Prescott has repeatedly spoken about how central fatherhood is to his life.

“I’m blessed to have the opportunity to raise two girls,” Prescott said in 2025. “It’s just about being grateful and not taking a moment for granted when I’m with them.”

His National Daughter’s Day post followed that same theme. There was no reference to Ramos , no mention of the allegations and no attempt to address the public fallout. Instead, Prescott kept the focus entirely on his daughters.

articles.title: Dak Prescott can't hide his frustration after the Cowboys' painful loss in Rio
articles.standfirst: Dak Prescott’s frustration boils over after Cowboys collapse against Ravens in Brazil
articles.summary: Dak Prescott’s frustration boils over after Cowboys collapse against Ravens in Brazil
articles.body:
Dak Prescot t couldn’t hide his frustration after the Dallas Cowboys suffered a painful 34-31 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in a thrilling game played Sunday night in Brazil.

Dak Prescott takes the blame: “We have to finish games”

Prescott and the Dallas offense managed to tie the game 31-31 in the final minutes , but Baltimore responded with a final drive that put Tyler Loop in position to hit a 56-yard field goal and give the Ravens the victory.

After the game, the quarterback reflected on the loss and, instead of pointing fingers, took responsibility alongside the offense for failing to close out the game in the most important moments.

“I’m sure when we land I’ll be just as pissed. This one hurts,” Prescott said.

“Frustrated as hell. Excuse me. Embarrassed. We know we call ourselves the best offense, GOTI, and we get down to the one-yard line and don’t put it in. Yeah, it just sucks. Not a lot of words or a full explanation for it. The defense shouldn’t even have been in that position. Those guys over there are saying it’s on us. Absolutely not. We’ve got to put the game away. Period.”

How Dak Prescott and the Cowboys performed against the Ravens

Dallas delivered a true battle against Baltimore and came within seconds of leaving Brazil with a victory. While fans enjoyed an emotional showdown, the Cowboys will return home feeling like they let a major opportunity slip away.

Both teams traded offensive blows throughout all four quarters and kept the game tied until the final moments. With the score knotted at 31-31, Tyler Loop stepped up and connected on his 56-yard kick to prevent overtime and give the Ravens the win.

Prescott did not have his best statistical performance through the air, as Dallas’ rushing attack played a key role. The quarterback completed 25 of 40 passes for 276 yards and one touchdown, while also adding 19 rushing yards on four carries.

Running back Javonte Williams led the ground game with 19 carries for 98 yards and a touchdown, while CeeDee Lamb was the top receiving target with seven catches for 112 yards . George Pickens also finished with seven receptions for 82 yards .

Now, the Cowboys will look to bounce back in Week 4 as they continue their road stretch against the Houston Texans . The matchup is scheduled for October 4 at 1:00 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Jerry Jones is sick of losing and wants to sign a key defensive player who will improve the Cowboys
articles.standfirst: The Dallas Cowboys slipped to a 34-31 defeat to the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday, September 27.
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys slipped to a 34-31 defeat to the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday, September 27.
articles.body:
J erry Jones has made it clear that the Dallas Cowboys are prepared to spend to strengthen their defense, and a reported interest in the Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. could give him another opportunity to do so. The Cowboys have spent the past year reshaping their defense, but injuries and inconsistencies in the secondary have once again exposed an area the franchise has been determined to improve after a 34-31 defeat to the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday.

And that search has reportedly brought Dallas into the picture for Porter Jr. , with the NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reporting that the Cowboys and Detroit Lions have inquired about the fourth-year defensive back. “The plot thickens: A few teams, including the #Lions and #Cowboys, have begun to inquire about the status of #Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr., per @AdamSchefter,” Rapoport said via X.com, formerly known as Twitter. Pittsburgh is reportedly willing to listen to offers for Porter , although the Steelers are seeking significant compensation for a player they still view as an important part of their defense and the situation has become complicated by his contract status. The cornerback is seeking a new deal, but Pittsburgh traditionally does not negotiate extensions once the regular season begins. With the two sides unable to reach an agreement during the offseason, a potential trade has emerged as a possibility. Porter has also yet to play this season and was inactive against the Cincinnati Bengals on September 27 after being limited in practice, although he insists he will be on the field as soon as he feels healthy enough to do so. Dallas has a clear reason to explore the market as Cobie Durant , who was expected to start at cornerback, missed Week 3 against the Ravens because of a hamstring injury, forcing the Cowboys to turn to practice squad activations to cope. Porter would represent a significant addition, but the potential cost could make the decision more complicated. Previous reports have indicated that Pittsburgh could seek a Day 1 draft pick but this is tricky for Jones . Dallas has already invested substantial draft capital in trades whilst the Cowboys also face a contract decision if they acquire Porter as the cornerback's asking price could be substantial. Notably, his fellow cornerback Trent McDuffie signed a four-year, $124 million deal with the Los Angeles Rams whilst Christian Gonzalez penned a four-year $135m deal with the New England Patriots .

Who do the Dallas Cowboys play next?

After slipping to the Ravens by way of Tyler Loop ’s late field goal for the AFC North side, the Cowboys are now 1-2 and threaten to be left behind by Eagles should Philadelphia beat the Chicago Bears on September 28’s Monday Night Football . A victory for the Eagles would see them take control of the AFC East by one game ahead of the New York Giants , and they would move to be two wins clear of the Cowboys which would make overturning the gap a difficult challenge for Dallas . The Cowboys will look to get back to winning ways on Sunday, October 4 against a Houston Texans side known for their defensive capabilities, although they have been beaten by the Buffalo Bills , Bengals and Indianapolis Colts . Kick off from 13:00 ET/10:00 PT and fans of both the Cowboys and AFC South ’s Texans can watch the game live on FOX Sports , with streaming available via the FOX Sports App , NFL+ and NFL Sunday Ticket . Highlights will be available via NFL RedZone .

articles.title: The Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders take Brazil by storm, but Dak Prescott ends up furious
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys brought the star power to Brazil, but Baltimore delivered the final blow
articles.summary: The Cowboys brought the star power to Brazil, but Baltimore delivered the final blow
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders took Brazil by storm before the Cowboys’ dramatic clash with the Baltimore Ravens , bringing their trademark energy to Rio de Janeiro while Dak Prescott and his teammates prepared for a night they won’t soon forget.

With both teams entering the Week 3 international matchup at 1-1, attention naturally centered on the players. However, the Cowboys Cheerleaders quickly became a major part of the spectacle surrounding the game at the iconic Maracanã Stadium.

The squad embraced its Brazilian adventure, sharing glimpses of Rio’s landmarks, rehearsals and preparations for the matchup.

They explored the city, posed at some of its famous locations and gave fans plenty of behind-the-scenes content as they adjusted to a very different game-day environment.

The cheerleaders also teamed up with Brazilian dancers for a preview of the halftime entertainment, combining the familiar Cowboys brand with local Brazilian flair. Their appearance quickly attracted attention online, with Flamengo sharing footage of the squad taking part in a dance challenge in Rio.

The Cowboys weren’t the only team represented away from the field. Baltimore’s cheerleaders participated in an NFL Flag Football clinic, giving young girls in Brazil an opportunity to step onto the field, learn about the sport and experience some of the excitement surrounding the NFL’s international visit.

The atmosphere was electric, but the evening ultimately ended very differently for Dallas’ biggest stars.

A spectacular finish leaves Prescott furious

The Cowboys appeared to have rescued the game when Brandon Aubrey converted a 23-yard field goal with seven seconds remaining, tying Baltimore 31-31. With virtually no time left, overtime looked like the obvious outcome.

Instead, Lamar Jackson immediately changed the script. Dallas sent the kickoff into the end zone for a touchback, giving Baltimore possession at its own 35-yard line with seven seconds remaining.

Jackson then delivered under pressure, completing a 27-yard pass to Zay Flowers. Flowers got out of bounds, allowing the Ravens to stop the clock with one second remaining. Tyler Loop stepped onto the field and drilled a 56-yard field goal as time expired, giving Baltimore a stunning 34-31 victory.

The kick was especially significant for Loop , whose last-second miss against Pittsburgh in Baltimore’s previous season finale had ended the Ravens’ playoff hopes. This time, he became the hero, celebrating with Cristiano Ronaldo’s famous “Siu” celebration before being lifted by his teammates.

Prescott , meanwhile, was left visibly frustrated. After the game, the Cowboys quarterback said he was “frustrated as hell” and “embarrassed,” emphasizing that Dallas had opportunities to close out the contest but failed to do so.

"Frustrated," Prescott said after the loss. "Frustrated as hell. Excuse me. Embarrassed. We don't call ourselves the best offense, GOTI, and get down to the one-yard line and don't put it in. Yeah, it just sucks.

“Not a lot of words or full explanation of it. Defense shouldn't even have been in that position. Those guys were over there saying 'it's on us,' absolutely not. We've got to put the game away, period."

Despite the painful defeat, Prescott praised the experience of playing in Brazil. The Cowboys now return home at 1-2, while the Ravens leave Rio with one of the most dramatic victories of the young season.

articles.title: NBC’s Mike Tomlin doesn’t hold back, labels Cowboys’ final sequence vs. Ravens ‘negligent’
articles.standfirst: Cowboys’ late-game decisions come under scrutiny after Ravens escape with dramatic victory
articles.summary: Cowboys’ late-game decisions come under scrutiny after Ravens escape with dramatic victory
articles.body:
Mike Tomlin didn’t hold back when discussing the Dallas Cowboys’ dramatic 34-31 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Brazil, taking particular aim at the team’s defensive strategy during the final seconds of regulation.

The former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach, now an NBC analyst, focused on Dallas’ decision to use man coverage with Baltimore needing only a modest gain to put itself in position for a game-winning field goal.

Tomlin described the sequence as “somewhat negligent” and said he was “really surprised” that the Cowboys opted for man-to-man coverage in that situation.

“I thought the sequence play by the Dallas Cowboys at the end of the game was somewhat negligent, to be quite honest with you,” said Tomlin .

Dallas had just tied the game at 31-31 on Brandon Aubrey’s 23-yard field goal, leaving seven seconds on the clock. The Cowboys then elected to kick the ball through the end zone rather than forcing Baltimore to return it. The resulting touchback gave the Ravens possession at their own 35-yard line without any time coming off the clock.

The decision was intended to prevent a dangerous return while forcing Lamar Jackson to make a difficult throw with very little time remaining. However, Baltimore quickly found a way to exploit the Cowboys’ defensive setup.

Cowboys’ late decisions opened the door

Tomlin explained that Dallas should’ve considered an “umbrella zone” in the situation, with defenders positioned deep enough to prevent an immediate completion from producing the yardage required for a long field-goal attempt.

Instead, Jackson found Zay Flowers for a 27-yard completion. Flowers was tackled at the Dallas 38-yard line, but the play left Baltimore with enough time to attempt a field goal. Jackson called the Ravens’ final timeout with one second remaining, allowing kicker Tyler Loop to come onto the field.

Loop calmly converted a 56-yard attempt as time expired, handing Baltimore the victory and leaving Dallas with a 1-2 record.

Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer defended the thinking behind the kickoff decision, explaining that Dallas wanted to force Baltimore to start at the 35 and then make a short completion rather than risk a return that could've changed the game immediately.

“We felt like, let’s boom it through, put them out there, make them throw the ball short and we’ll be fine,” Schottenheimer said. “Play for overtime. That’s what the plan was.”

The defensive call, however, left Dallas vulnerable to exactly the type of big play it was trying to prevent. Flowers won his matchup, and Jackson delivered the ball accurately enough to put Baltimore in scoring range.

The Cowboys also had opportunities to avoid the frantic finish altogether. After falling behind 24-13 in the third quarter, Dak Prescott led a strong comeback that brought Dallas level. Later, the Cowboys reached Baltimore’s 2-yard line with 23 seconds remaining but failed to score a touchdown.

Dallas settled for Aubrey’s field goal, leaving the Ravens just enough time to respond. A combination of the kickoff decision, defensive coverage and earlier clock-management choices ultimately proved costly.

articles.title: Trouble for the Cowboys over cheerleaders' “wild” party in Brazil after losing to the Ravens
articles.standfirst: Dallas fell 34-31 to the Ravens in dramatic fashion, but the franchise’s cheer squad still produced one of the highlights of the weekend
articles.summary: Dallas fell 34-31 to the Ravens in dramatic fashion, but the franchise’s cheer squad still produced one of the highlights of the weekend
articles.body:
The final seconds in Rio could hardly have been more painful for the Dallas Cowboys . Moments after Brandon Aubrey tied the game against the Baltimore Ravens , Dallas appeared to be heading toward overtime.

Instead, the Ravens produced a stunning final sequence, moved into field-goal range almost immediately and watched Tyler Loop kick the winning 56-yarder as time expired.

The 34-31 defeat left the Cowboys at 1-2 and sent the team home from Brazil with the kind of loss that can linger long after the flight lands. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer admitted as much afterward.

“At the end of the day, I just really just feel bad for [the players],” he said. “You know, we played hard, we fought back, after a long trip, and we had our chance to win. Unfortunately, we didn’t get it done.”

There was, however, another side to the Cowboys ’ trip. While the football team was left processing a heartbreaking finish, the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders made the most of the franchise’s visit to Rio and played a major role in the atmosphere surrounding the game.

Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders embrace Brazil spotlight

The squad performed its famous “Thunderstruck” routine in front of a packed Brazilian crowd, bringing one of the franchise’s most recognizable traditions to the international stage.

Their performance was one of the major entertainment moments of the night and gave local fans a glimpse of the full Cowboys game-day experience.

The cheerleaders also had the chance to be part of a high-profile halftime show featuring Ricky Martin , adding another memorable moment to a trip that had already generated considerable attention.

Throughout the visit, the group embraced the occasion and the energy surrounding the NFL’s growing presence in Brazil. The contrast between the celebration in the stands and the heartbreak on the field could hardly have been sharper.

Schottenheimer turns attention back to Dallas

The Cowboys still have plenty to address after letting a winnable game slip away in dramatic fashion. Schottenheimer made clear that responsibility would be shared across the organization.

“No one can say that they called or played a perfect game. No one,” he said. “And so, to me, at the end of the day, we all look at ourselves first. We pull our bootstraps up, we get our asses back to Frisco, and we go back to work.”

Dallas will now try to regroup after falling below .500, while Baltimore leaves Brazil at 2-1 after producing one of the most dramatic finishes of the season.

The Cowboys cheerleaders, though, will have a different set of memories from the trip.

Their time in Brazil featured packed stands, a marquee halftime performance and the chance to showcase one of the NFL’s most recognizable traditions on an international stage.

The result may have ruined the night for the Cowboys , but it did not stop their cheerleaders from making the most of Rio.

articles.title: A former Cowboys player retires at age 29 after keeping nerve issues secret during his career
articles.standfirst: A hidden spinal condition forced the former NFL linebacker to walk away from football
articles.summary: A hidden spinal condition forced the former NFL linebacker to walk away from football
articles.body:
Malik Jefferson has revealed that a serious neck and nerve condition helped bring his football career to an early end, announcing his retirement at 29 after years of playing through pain.

The former Dallas Cowboys linebacker shared the news on September 28, explaining that he’d spent much of his career dealing with injuries without fully understanding the underlying problem.

Jefferson said he eventually discovered that his C5-C7 vertebrae had been damaged and that he continues to deal with the consequences in his everyday life.

“For years, I didn’t know I was battling a nerve/neck issue,” Jefferson wrote on Instagram. “Constantly getting injuries, always in the training room, or doing extra rehab and mobility work. "Towards the end of my career, I kept playing through the pain of my arm going numb on impact. I couldn’t handle the pain anymore; it was 10/10.

“Fast forward, I discovered my C5-C7 has been damaged. Today I still suffer from those injuries and still struggle with my day to day so I’d really appreciate prayers! It’s not said enough: get pictures of your spine and neck consistently players!!”

Jefferson had previously discussed his medical problems while being recognized for his community work through his Helping Hands Foundation.

During that appearance, he explained that his retirement decision was medical and revealed additional health concerns, including hip problems that could eventually require replacement.

A promising career disrupted by injuries

Jefferson entered the NFL with significant expectations after starring at the University of Texas. He was named a Freshman All-American in 2015 and continued developing into one of the Big 12's standout defensive players.

During his final college season in 2017, he recorded 110 tackles, earned Big 12 Co-Defensive Player of the Year honors and received second-team All-American recognition.

He finished his Texas career with 233 tackles and 12 sacks before declaring for the 2018 NFL Draft. The Cincinnati Bengals selected him with the 78th overall pick, making him one of the more notable linebackers available that year.

However, Jefferson's professional career never developed into the extended run that his college production had suggested. He moved between several teams before eventually joining Dallas.

The Cowboys signed him in 2022, and he appeared in three games for the team during the 2023 season, recording three tackles.

Jefferson later signed with the Detroit Lions in 2024. After suffering a finger injury during the preseason, Detroit placed him on injured reserve before releasing him with an injury settlement.

articles.title: Dak Prescott's ex-girlfriend, Sarah Jane Ramos, lashes out at him again after publicly revealing the quarterback's infidelity
articles.standfirst: Prescott and Ramos continue co-parenting their two daughters after ending their engagement
articles.summary: Prescott and Ramos continue co-parenting their two daughters after ending their engagement
articles.body:
Sarah Jane Ramos appears to be turning to faith and family as she moves forward following the end of her engagement to Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott.

Ramos recently shared a photo on Instagram showing herself with the couple's two daughters at the beach, accompanied by a message about the importance of her family.

“A whole lot of love held together by Faith,” she wrote. “Our very solid little family. My girls, my rocks. Maybe the greatest thing I ever built was us.”

The post comes shortly after Ramos publicly addressed speculation about a possible pregnancy. She firmly denied the rumors and said she was happier after leaving a relationship in which she claimed she had been “cheated on repeatedly.”

The remarks have added to an already closely followed breakup between Ramos and Prescott . The couple called off their planned April wedding in Lake Como, Italy, in March, just weeks before they were due to marry.

At the time, a representative for Ramos described the decision as mutual and said there hadn't been a major argument or dramatic incident immediately before the split.

Ramos and Prescott appear focused on their daughters

Reports later linked the breakup to allegations involving Prescott's communications with other women, although those reports remain allegations and the circumstances surrounding the split have been described differently by people connected to the former couple.

Prescott eventually addressed the breakup publicly in August, saying there had been “false narratives” on both sides.

Rather than going into detail about the relationship, he emphasized his responsibility toward their children and said his priority was being there for them.

Ramos ' latest comments also don't necessarily signal a complete breakdown in their relationship as co-parents.

According to a source cited by People, she still has love for Prescott , and the former couple remain friends while raising their two daughters, Margaret Jane Rose and Aurora Rayne.

“Sarah Jane also wants it understood that she and Dak are friends. They share two beautiful children and they have a tremendous amount of history,” the source noted.

“His actions were affecting her to a point where she felt both of them were unhappy. The timing of their breakup was not ideal, but Sarah Jane and Dak were not at a time or place where they felt like they could move forward.”

The former couple have continued to put their daughters at the center of their lives despite the end of their engagement.

Prescott has also made clear that the children are the most important consideration as both parents navigate the fallout from their separation.

Ramos appears to be concentrating on her family and moving ahead with her life, while Prescott remains focused on his career with the Cowboys. Their relationship may have ended, but their responsibilities as parents continue to keep them connected.

articles.title: Jerry Jones delivers a blunt message to Dak Prescott and the Cowboys after last-second loss to Ravens
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys lost because they let the Ravens get a field goal try with seven seconds left in regulation
articles.summary: The Cowboys lost because they let the Ravens get a field goal try with seven seconds left in regulation
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL season has delivered relentless drama through the opening weeks, highlighted by a staggering Week 3 , when 12 of the 14 Sunday game s were decided by a single possession..

Among the most electrifying spectacles was a historic matchup between the Dallas Cowboys and the Baltimore Ravens , giving more than 70,000 fans a heart-stopping finish.

Regulation concluded with a dramatic 56-yard field goal from Ravens kicker Tyler Loop as time expired, sealing a 34-31 victory and sparking celebrations featuring an iconic " Siuuu" tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo .

The Cowboys appeared poised for a dramatic comeback after driving to the 2-yard line with just 23 seconds remaining and a single timeout left, but they ultimately opted for a short field goal to knot the score at 31-31 .

That decision left 7 precious seconds on the game clock, plenty of time for Lamar Jackson to hook up with Zay Flowers on a crucial 27-yard completion that set up Loop's walk-off heroics.

Jerry Jones Delivers Blunt Warning as Cowboys Face Early-Season Adversity

Dropping to a 1-2 record marks the third consecutive year Dallas has stumbled out of the gate with a losing ledger through three weeks, placing mounting pressure on the front office, head coach Brian Schottenheimer , and quarterback Dak Prescott .

Speaking bluntly on 105.3 The Fan's Shan and RJ show , owner Jerry Jones dismissed any room for sugarcoating after squandering a prime opportunity against Baltimore. "There is no explanation that you’re satisfied with. None. Let’s be sure that we all understand that," Jones stated.

"We made mistakes during that time, there’s no question about it. There’s no explanation. There’s an evaluation of how to not make the same mistakes again, which is what you should be doing."

Despite the frustrating skid, Jones emphasized that the division race remains wide open given early stumbles and injuries across the NFC East , adding, "We are very much in the hunt. We’re just getting started. ... We will be better because of the experience that we had with Baltimore and what happened to us at the end of the game."

Ahead of a demanding October schedule , Dallas must quickly shore up its defensive vulnerabilities. The schedule starts with a matchup against the 0-3 Houston Texans on Sunday.

Then, the team will face three straight primetime games : a Thursday night home game against the now 0-3 Tampa Bay Buccaneers , a Sunday night trip to Green Bay , and a Monday night game in Philadelphia .

Starting November with a winning record would be a major positive, but first, Dallas has to improve considerably on defense.

articles.title: Brian Schottenheimer steps up and takes blame for late-game Cowboys failure
articles.standfirst: The Ravens beat the Cowboys 34-31 in Rio de Janeiro on a 56-yard field goal from Tyler Loop, but the aftermath belongs to Brian Schottenheimer.
articles.summary: The Ravens beat the Cowboys 34-31 in Rio de Janeiro on a 56-yard field goal from Tyler Loop, but the aftermath belongs to Brian Schottenheimer.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens pulled off a dramatic win over the Dallas Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro , in a game decided in the final seconds. With the score tied late, Lamar Jackson connected with Zay Flowers on a 27-yard pass that put Baltimore in field goal range, and Tyler Loop answered with a 56-yard kick to seal the 34-31 win.

After the loss, Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer took responsibility for the mistakes in the final seconds and admitted his decisions hurt Dallas' chances.

"I didn't do very good in the final 20 seconds (of Sunday's game in Rio). … I hurt our chances to win that game. I'm better than that. … Those things won't happen again."

Dallas came up just short of the end zone

The sequence that defined the game began with the Cowboys ' last offensive drive of the fourth quarter. Dallas reached the red zone and got as far as the Baltimore 5-yard line, but couldn't find the touchdown that would have secured the win.

Schottenheimer explained that the plan was to score and close out the game, though he admitted the execution fell short.

"Yeah, we thought we were going to score a touchdown. We thought we were going to score a touchdown and move the ball really well down there. We've got to find a way to punch it in. I've got to call some better plays to get it in."

The defensive plan: play for overtime

The coach also revealed that the defensive idea was to concede a short pass and, if they couldn't stop the Ravens, go to overtime.

"We felt like, let's boom it through, put them out there, make them throw the ball short, and we'll be fine," Schottenheimer said. "Play for overtime. That's what the plan was."

Schottenheimer also defended the decision to use man coverage on Baltimore's final possession, a call that let Lamar Jackson find Zay Flowers at the Dallas 38-yard line to set up the winning field goal.

"I liked the [defensive] call. We wanted to stay sticky. But at the end of the day, they ran two ins. It's actually a play we run quite a bit of. The bottom line is you've got to make the ball go to the first one, not the layer that they hit to Zay Flowers. That's where we have to be better."

articles.title: Jerry Jones shakes up free agency: Two new defensive players to help the Cowboys
articles.standfirst: Juanyeh Thomas is back in Dallas, while Alex Austin joins the practice squad
articles.summary: Juanyeh Thomas is back in Dallas, while Alex Austin joins the practice squad
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys have reached the point where depth in the secondary is no longer a luxury. Injuries have stripped away several of the team’s preferred options at safety and cornerback, forcing Dallas to search for immediate help.

That search led to a pair of moves Tuesday, with the Cowboys agreeing to terms with Juanyeh Thomas and Alex Austin after working out multiple defensive backs.

Thomas returns to an organization he already knows well, while Austin gives Dallas another experienced cornerback to develop on the practice squad. The additions come with the Cowboys trying to stabilize a defensive backfield that has been hit from almost every direction.

Malik Hooker is recovering from a fractured forearm, P.J. Locke is on injured reserve because of a foot injury and Jalen Thompson is expected to join him after suffering a hamstring problem. Shavon Revel and Cobie Durant are also dealing with injuries at cornerback.

Juanyeh Thomas gives Dallas much-needed familiarity

Thomas may be the more immediately useful addition because he already understands the organization and has spent significant time in a Cowboys uniform.

The former Georgia Tech safety originally joined Dallas as an undrafted free agent in 2022, spent time on the practice squad and eventually worked his way into the defensive rotation. He has appeared in 36 NFL games, totaling 62 tackles, five passes defensed and one forced fumble.

His role gradually grew during his first stint. Thomas played 190 defensive snaps in 2023, added 94 more in 2024 and then logged 266 snaps across seven games with three starts last season.

Special teams were also a major part of his value, with Thomas recording more than 700 snaps in that phase from 2023 through 2025. That versatility could be particularly useful for a Cowboys team trying to cover multiple absences at once.

Dallas allowed Thomas to leave during the offseason after declining to tender him as a restricted free agent. He signed with Indianapolis but was released in August after migraine problems affected him during training camp.

Alex Austin adds more depth

Austin brings a different profile but valuable NFL experience. A seventh-round pick by Buffalo in 2023, the cornerback has played 29 games with six starts while spending time with New England and Houston .

He has recorded 31 tackles, eight passes defensed and one interception during his career.

The Cowboys also evaluated Shemar Bartholomew, Tyrek Funderburk and linebacker Germaine Pratt during Tuesday’s workout as they looked for ways to reinforce a defense dealing with a growing number of injuries.

Thomas and Austin don't erase those problems, but they give Dallas more options at a point when the depth chart has become increasingly fragile.

Thomas offers familiarity, special-teams experience and previous starting snaps in Dallas, while Austin gives the Cowboys another cornerback who has already played meaningful NFL football.

The immediate challenge is simply getting through the next stretch without the secondary unraveling.

These moves are less about making a splash and more about survival, and with so many defensive backs unavailable, that may be exactly what Dallas needs most right now.

articles.title: Jerry Jones wants to give Brian Schottenheimer new tools to turn season around and admits negotiations are underway
articles.standfirst: The defense has struggled despite heavy investment
articles.summary: The defense has struggled despite heavy investment
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys have spent much of the past year rebuilding a defense that failed to meet expectations, yet three games into the 2026 NFL season the work is clearly not finished.

Dallas enters Week 4 at 1-2 after a painful loss to Baltimore Ravens in Rio de Janeiro, and injuries have only complicated matters.

The secondary has been hit particularly hard, while the defense as a whole has struggled despite a series of high-profile additions. That has pushed Jerry Jones back into the trade market.

“We’re right on top of it,” Jones said during his weekly appearance on 105.3 The Fan. “We’re very aware of the moving parts out here. We should be. And communication is a big part of that.

“The answer to your question is, yes, there’s conversations going on,” Jones added. “Not specific to the player you just mentioned… Trying to avoid tampering here, folks.”

Joey Porter Jr. hanging over conversation

The player Jones was being asked about was Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. , who has reportedly drawn interest from Dallas and Detroit.

Porter has missed the first three games of the season with a back issue, but he was a full participant in practice Monday and could be moving closer to a return. His contract situation, however, may be just as important as his health.

The 25-year-old is in the final year of his rookie deal and is seeking a long-term extension. Pittsburgh has traditionally been reluctant to fully guarantee future salary beyond the first year of a contract, while Porter is believed to want stronger security.

That difference has fueled speculation that the Steelers could listen to serious offers. Porter has said publicly that he wants to play for Pittsburgh and has denied requesting a trade, but the Cowboys have obvious reasons to monitor the situation.

Dallas already spent heavily on defense

Jones hasn't been shy about trying to upgrade Brian Schottenheimer ’s roster.

Dallas has added Quinnen Williams, Rashan Gary and Kenny Clark through trades while also using premium draft capital on Caleb Downs and Malachi Lawrence . Even with those moves, the Cowboys entered Week 4 ranked 30th in total defense.

Injuries have made the problem worse. Cobie Durant is dealing with a hamstring issue, while Dallas has also been forced to dig deeper into its secondary depth.

Jones has already made clear that money won't stop him if he believes the right move is available.

“We have the makings of a team here that I’m that optimistic about, and would work to improve it in a minute, right now, financially,” Jones said previously.

The bigger complication is draft capital. Dallas has already used significant future assets in previous deals, meaning another major trade would require careful calculation.

Any move for Porter would likely involve both valuable picks and a substantial extension afterward. That makes the next decision one of balance rather than ambition.

Jones clearly still believes this team can turn its season around. The question is whether the Cowboys are willing to spend again to give Schottenheimer one more major piece.

articles.title: Dallas Cowboys turn to AI to tackle a game-day frustration fans know too well
articles.standfirst: AT&T’s latest technology could change how Cowboys fans experience game day
articles.summary: AT&T’s latest technology could change how Cowboys fans experience game day
articles.body:
Leaving your seat for food at an NFL game comes with an uncomfortable calculation: is there enough time to grab something and get back before the next big play? The Dallas Cowboys want technology inside AT&T Stadium to help fans make that decision with more information and less guesswork.

According to Inc ., the Cowboys are working with AT&T’s Proof of Concept Labs on dynamic stadium signage. Screens could display concession wait times and indicate how much time fans have to return to their seats during commercial breaks. They would also help visitors find their way around the venue and provide scores, statistics and weather updates.

How the Cowboys want AI to change the stadium experience

The idea is to make screens more useful at each stage of a visit. Directions matter when people arrive or leave; during a break in the action, the more pressing question may be whether a food line is worth joining. Zee Hussain, senior vice president of Global Enterprise Solutions at AT&T Business, told Inc. that artificial intelligence is helping signage evolve beyond historically static displays. However, the report does not specify a stadium-wide launch date for every function described.

Other additions have already been announced for the 2026 season. AT&T and the Cowboys extended their partnership in September, outlining navigation tools accessible through the Cowboys app and stadium kiosks. The announcement also introduced Starbase Connection, an AI-powered feature that turns photos submitted by fans into personalized Cowboys hype videos displayed on stadium boards.

That gives the technology two distinct roles: helping people move through the stadium and bringing them into its entertainment. Fans can also use augmented reality to create photos with Cowboys players, legends and cheerleaders, while a mixed-reality attraction lets them catch virtual passes from Dak Prescott . These are separate experiences from the proposed concession and commercial-break information, even though they depend on the same broader connectivity investment.

Making those experiences work requires more than an impressive screen. AT&T says the venue supports approximately 22 terabytes of data traffic on an average game day, with more than 90,000 fans attending. Its network supports mobile ticket scanning, concessions, apps and operational systems, alongside approximately 3,500 televisions and 3,000 Wi-Fi access points. Two independent network paths allow traffic to be rerouted if one is disrupted.

The testing behind that infrastructure is where the laboratory enters the story. Established in 1996, AT&T’s Proof of Concept Labs now supports more than 500 enterprise customers annually , according to the company. Businesses can evaluate applications and network configurations before deploying them in live environments, where a failure could interrupt service or operations. The program has expanded from early networking tests into areas including 5G, security and networks supporting AI.

For the Cowboys, AT&T specifically confirms testing a public 5G solution that gives critical event operations a prioritized lane on the network . That work addresses activities extending beyond the stadium into surrounding areas where traditional Wi-Fi may not reach. It is intended to inform future deployments as the team’s event footprint grows.

For fans, the practical test will be straightforward: does the technology make attending a game easier? A personalized video offers a memorable moment. Reliable directions and useful information about a concession line could have a more immediate payoff helping someone return to their seat in time to see the play they came for.

Zee Hussain, senior vice president of Global Enterprise Solutions at AT&T Business, told Inc. that artificial intelligence is helping signage evolve beyond historically static displays. However, the report does not specify a stadium-wide launch date for every function described.

Other additions have already been announced for the 2026 season. AT&T and the Cowboys extended their partnership in September, outlining navigation tools accessible through the Cowboys app and stadium kiosks. The announcement also introduced Starbase Connection, an AI-powered feature that turns photos submitted by fans into personalized Cowboys hype videos displayed on stadium boards.

That gives the technology two distinct roles: helping people move through the stadium and bringing them into its entertainment. Fans can also use augmented reality to create photos with Cowboys players, legends and cheerleaders, while a mixed-reality attraction lets them catch virtual passes from Dak Prescott . These are separate experiences from the proposed concession and commercial-break information, even though they depend on the same broader connectivity investment.

Making those experiences work requires more than an impressive screen. AT&T says the venue supports approximately 22 terabytes of data traffic on an average game day, with more than 90,000 fans attending. Its network supports mobile ticket scanning, concessions, apps and operational systems, alongside approximately 3,500 televisions and 3,000 Wi-Fi access points. Two independent network paths allow traffic to be rerouted if one is disrupted.

The testing behind that infrastructure is where the laboratory enters the story. Established in 1996, AT&T’s Proof of Concept Labs now supports more than 500 enterprise customers annually , according to the company. Businesses can evaluate applications and network configurations before deploying them in live environments, where a failure could interrupt service or operations. The program has expanded from early networking tests into areas including 5G, security and networks supporting AI.

For the Cowboys, AT&T specifically confirms testing a public 5G solution that gives critical event operations a prioritized lane on the network . That work addresses activities extending beyond the stadium into surrounding areas where traditional Wi-Fi may not reach. It is intended to inform future deployments as the team’s event footprint grows.

For fans, the practical test will be straightforward: does the technology make attending a game easier? A personalized video offers a memorable moment. Reliable directions and useful information about a concession line could have a more immediate payoff helping someone return to their seat in time to see the play they came for.
